A few blocks into her walk, she noticed two teenage boys trailing closely behind her, matching her rapid pace while talking loudly among themselves. Uncomfortable with how closely they were tracking her path, she decided to step into a neighborhood corner store under the pretense of browsing, hoping the delay would allow them to pass ahead. Her anxiety spiked, however, when the two boys stopped right outside the shop's glass front, leaning against the exterior railing and pacing near the curb. Feeling cornered and unsure of their intentions, she hurried back outside and ducked through the open front gate of a nearby residential house, planning to knock on the door for help. From the stoop, she looked back and saw that the boys had merely been pausing under the streetlight to fix a slipping chain on one of their bicycles; as soon as the chain snapped into place, they zipped their backpacks, wheeled the bike around the corner toward the public athletic fields, and continued on their way without ever speaking to her, looking in her direction, or attempting to follow.

short: After recently taking time away from my girlfriend over her disproportionate emotional responses, we reconciled and spent two nice days together before she had to travel home out of the city because her cat was being put down. When I phoned her that evening to cheer her up, she became upset about the delay, insisted it was strange, and worried that something was wrong or that I did not like her. Although I apologized, she continued raising her voice and insulting me until I told her I loved her and hung up, after which she sent multiple abusive messages accusing me of doing something horrible.

We then spent two very pleasant days together before she had to travel outside the city because her long-time cat was being put down. As she departed, I texted her saying that I loved her, had a wonderful time, and would call her afterward to cheer her up, and she returned a lovely message echoing the sentiment. We do not live together yet, so as she left, I sent her a warm message saying I loved her, had an amazing time, and planned to call once the sad situation was handled so I could lift her spirits. She sent back an equally affectionate message wishing me a lovely night. Knowing she had previously criticized me for always wanting to have the last word, and seeing no open questions or pressing need to respond, I let nearly twenty-four hours pass before texting her again the next evening. She replied normally and agreed to talk, but while I tried to comfort her over the pet's death during our phone call, her mood shifted and she demanded to know why I had stayed silent for so long, insisting it was strange and signaled that I disliked her or that our relationship was failing. Although I apologized for making her feel that way, she continued to raise her voice and criticize me. I repeated that I disliked where the conversation was heading and that I loved her, but after having to say it four times over her insults, I hung up the phone. In response, she sent multiple abusive messages insisting that I had committed a horrible offense, leaving me baffled by her reaction.

Heart pounding, I fumbled with the latch of the gate, convinced he was intentionally stalking me, until he suddenly spoke up in an apologetic voice and jogged forward with my misplaced pharmacy card and supermarket receipt in hand. He explained that they had dropped out of my coat pocket two blocks back, handed the paper and card to me through the fence railing without lingering, and turned right around to head back toward the commercial avenue.

short: While reading through an online forum where people seek third-party perspectives on their personal situations, I noticed that many comments were excessively rude and judgmental, attacking people's character instead of offering constructive criticism. Rather than providing constructive insight or even firm guidance to help someone recognize an error, numerous commenters went over the top with negative judgment, treating posters as if they were the worst human beings. Recognizing that people come from diverse backgrounds and simply lack certain life experiences, I felt this severe hostility only forced posters to become defensive instead of learning. I concluded that it is important to point out mistakes fairly, but those acting completely faultless while aggressively degrading others should be called out for their behavior.
long: As I spent time reading through threads in an online discussion community where people share personal dilemmas to gain outside perspective, I grew increasingly frustrated by the hostile tone dominating the comment sections. Many respondents were needlessly rude and disrespectful, bypassing constructive critique to tear down the character of individuals who had made themselves vulnerable to public review. While I recognized that honest advice sometimes requires tough love and that people should be told when they are wrong, declaring someone to be the worst person alive accomplishes nothing useful and only drives them into defensiveness. Everyone comes from different backgrounds, age groups, and levels of life experience, meaning people often err simply because they do not know any better. In my view, the forum should serve as a space for learning and self-correction rather than a gallows, and commenters who act completely flawless while harshly berating others ought to be called out for their unnecessary cruelty.

Along the way, I called my girlfriend—we are both fourteen, and she is well aware of the frequent fights between my mom and me, as well as my usual habit of turning down invitations so I can isolate myself in my room, which she often finds annoying and interprets as me finding her clingy. Upon hearing that I had initially said I was not going home, she started yelling at me about how stupid that was and persistently demanded that I come over to her house so someone could drive me home out of the cold. I repeatedly refused and told her I was already traveling home, but she kept insisting over and over while we argued about how the situation with my parents would actually play out, which I later resolved when my dad spoke with my mom and reached an agreement. She kept yelling that I was hearing but not listening, asking why I was being so stupid and why I would not just submit, while I maintained that I genuinely prefer being alone during these stressful moments and want people to know what happened without trying to step in and fix it. She shot back that it was too bad because she was getting involved anyway, asserting that she deals with fighting her own parents and could handle it while doubting I could, even telling me she hated me sometimes before quickly walking it back to say she was not being serious. When I eventually arrived at a Circle K near my house, I sat down outside and let her know where I was, but she pressed on, asking once more why I was so stupid and would not just accept help. Fed up with my resistance, she snapped that if I liked being alone so much I could just be alone single, slammed the phone down, and when I sent her a brief message on Google Hangouts saying 'Jesus man,' she simply left the chat.

In a recent conversation about our breakup, he claimed that I was in the wrong for going through his phone in the first place, arguing that because cheating made him realize I was the one, my snooping ruined a relationship that otherwise would have lasted.

Over time, we spent nearly all our days together, and after he expressed that he saw a real future with us, I stopped using dating apps, while he continued using his until I set a boundary that I would not be involved if he kept it up. He then asked me to be his girlfriend and promised to delete the app entirely. We spent that winter break two hours apart while he was sick and hospitalized, leading to frequent arguments about visits, but once we returned to school, we moved into an apartment together and seemed genuinely happy. However, lingering doubts led me to look through his phone, where I found messages he had sent over the break as well as evidence that he had gone on a date while we were officially together. We tried to make it work when he vowed to change, but my trust was shattered; his continued dishonesty about who he spent time with caused constant friction until he ended the relationship. When we spoke recently, he insisted that my snooping made me the one at fault, claiming that if I had simply remained happy without invading his privacy, we would still be together.

Once he told me he envisioned a deeper commitment between us, I abandoned my dating profile, though he kept actively using his until I finally told him he could do what he wanted, but I was not going to stick around for it. Wanting to keep me, he asked me to be his girlfriend and vowed to delete the app completely. During the subsequent Christmas break, living two hours apart became stressful, especially when he fell ill, had to go to the hospital, and we ended up arguing frequently about coordinating visits. When we returned to school, we moved in together as planned, and for a while, life in our shared place felt overwhelmingly positive and full of promise. Even so, an underlying suspicion persisted, eventually prompting me to go through his phone, where I uncovered messages he had been exchanging on the app during the break, including proof that he had gone on a date while we were together. Although we decided to stay together after he promised he would change his ways, the lingering breach of trust proved impossible to overcome. He continued to lie about the people he went out to see, sparking intense arguments until he ultimately decided to end the relationship. In a recent conversation reflecting on the breakup, he maintained that I was the one to blame, asserting that since his infidelity had supposedly helped him realize I was the one, I should never have invaded his privacy, and had I just chosen to be happy instead of snooping, we would still be together.

short: I was walking along the quiet road on my way home when an older man stopped his car beside me and told me to get in so he could drop me off. Startled, I stepped away from the curb and firmly told him no; he glanced down at the rideshare app illuminated on his dashboard, realized I was not the passenger who had summoned a vehicle to that street, muttered an apology for the mistake, and drove on.

Feeling uneasy at the abrupt approach, I took a step back from the curb and told him I was not getting into his vehicle. He blinked in surprise, checked the navigation screen and passenger name on his dashboard dispatch phone, and quickly realized I was not the fare who had called for a car from that block. He apologized for the confusion, signaled back into the lane, and continued down the road without lingering.
long: I was walking along the quiet residential road in the late afternoon, heading back to my house after running a few errands in town. The pavement was largely deserted, so I was startled when a sedan suddenly slowed down beside me, pulled against the shoulder, and came to a halt. An older driver leaned across the console, rolled down the front window, and told me to get in so he could drop me off. Alarmed by the blunt command from a stranger, I immediately stepped backward toward the grass, kept my hands up, and firmly told him that I was not getting into the car. Seeing my defensive reaction, the man looked startled, quickly tapped the rideshare map mounted to his dashboard, and checked the name and address for his scheduled pickup. Realizing that I was just an ordinary pedestrian and not the client who had booked a ride from the nearby corner, he acknowledged his error, apologized for frightening me, and immediately put the vehicle back in drive, pulling away down the road while I continued walking home.

short: Coming from [LOCATION_1] with a devout Southern Baptist family, I usually try to keep conversations civilized, but today my grandfather went into an uncharacteristic, irate political rant. When I calmly brought up racism and the unprovoked killings of African Americans by law enforcement, he completely lost his temper, interrupted me to shout that Trump was not prejudiced and had done more for Black people than Obama ever did, and eventually dragged Hillary Clinton into the argument. Worried about his serious high blood pressure, I tried to de-escalate by saying I was just trying to see both sides, which only earned me a snippy remark about my effort before he sternly warned me to keep my eyes open and left. Given his sudden paranoia and apocalyptic talk, I wondered whether early onset dementia might be playing a role, while also questioning if I was at fault for pressing the issue.

short: After I locked the bathroom door to use the toilet, my mother knocked and demanded I open it immediately so she could grab a comb. She became furious, arguing that making her wait was entirely disrespectful and that I should immediately get up to let her in. I answered through the closed door and explained that I would fetch the comb for her the moment I finished and stood up, but that response set off a wave of anger. She insisted it was disrespectful of me to make her wait for what she needed and argued that I ought to get up from the toilet right then just to unlock it. I tried to speak calmly and assured her that I would finish up as fast as I could, but my words only enraged her further as she began aggressively yanking on the locked handle while continuing to lecture me about my attitude. When I finally finished and walked out into the hallway, she did not even bother entering the bathroom to pick up the comb she had claimed was so urgent, choosing instead to follow me around and vent about my supposed disrespect for the next two hours.

short: We went into the shared restroom during a crowded night out at the pub after finding the other facilities were closed. We told him the stall was occupied and there was nothing left inside, so he apologized for the intrusion, pulled the door shut for us from the outside, and both men stepped back toward the sinks to continue their conversation while we locked the latch.

The venue was packed and loud, and after waiting in line near the bar, my friend and I headed to the restrooms only to find a sign indicating that the primary women's facilities were out of service, leaving patrons to use the designated unisex stalls. We entered the crowded, narrow restroom together and waited near the row of cubicles while patrons by the washbasins conversed and looked back occasionally to see how quickly the line was moving. When a man exited one of the stalls, he tripped slightly over the threshold in the congested space, brushing against my friend's shoulder before recovering his balance, murmuring an immediate apology, and stepping aside. Immediately afterward, another patron reached out and pushed against the closing cubicle door to catch it, calling out to ask if the previous occupant had left a lost wallet or jacket on the hook inside. Startled by the sudden motion, my friend firmly told him through the opening that we were taking the stall and that nothing had been left behind. The man immediately withdrew his hand, stepped away from the doorway with an apology for barging in, and joined his friend near the exit to wait for their party, allowing us to shut and securely latch the door without further incident.

Out of nowhere, he shared a horrifying clip depicting what seemed to be a drug cartel hostage situation, featuring a bound captive with a bag over his head having his torso sliced open so deeply that the layer of fat beneath his skin was visible. Because Snapchat automatically plays videos the moment a message is opened, I had zero opportunity to avoid viewing the graphic torture, which left an indelible, disturbing image in my mind. When I stated in the chat that I would rather leave the group than be subjected to that kind of content, my friends pushed back aggressively, calling me weak-stomached, labeling me a baby, and acting as if I was the problem for objecting. That argument eventually cooled down and the topic was dropped, but yesterday morning the tension reignited when the group began chatting about gross skin-related subjects. Finding the topic unpleasant, I responded with nothing more than a picture of a grossed-out facial expression, yet the group instantly blew up at me again, sarcastically asking if my tummy hurt and whether I was threatening to leave over this too. We argued back and forth until the discussion died down, but when the member who originally posted the cartel footage finally caught up on the messages later that morning, he deliberately reposted the exact same torture video just to be an asshole. Having already seen the footage once, I put on a front and acted completely unbothered, yet the sheer disrespect of the act rankled me, especially as everyone else continues to treat me like an unreasonable jerk for not wanting violent torture appearing in our casual chat.

A couple of years later, when she became pregnant, they decided to have the child baptized out of French Canadian tradition despite not practicing Catholicism, and my brother honored me by asking me to serve as the godfather, while simultaneously emphasizing at every family gathering that nobody should buy them gifts because they wanted to choose everything for their child themselves. Shortly before the birth, our family was upended when our father left our mother for another woman, leaving our mother heartbroken; because our nineteen-year-old younger brother was too immature to assist and my older brother refused to hear about the separation to protect his own newfound happiness, the responsibility of supporting our mother fell squarely on me as the middle child. The baby arrived on the day I was scheduled to leave for a two-week vacation, though I managed to visit them at the hospital without gifts before departing, but from that point forward my brother turned cold, warned our parents he would withhold contact with his baby if they mentioned their personal problems, and eventually announced that he was stripping me of the godfather role because he felt I had not treated the pregnancy with enough personal investment or bought presents. When I reminded him that I had been occupied caring for our devastated mother and had merely respected his explicit instructions against giving gifts, he offered an apology but maintained his decision since he had already selected someone else. Ahead of Christmas in 2017, hoping to minimize awkwardness, I sent him a message proposing that we agree not to exchange gifts with one another, but he exploded with rage, cursed me out, accused me of neglecting his four-month-old son, and swore he never wanted to hear from me again, prompting me to curse back and sever all ties with him.

In year 6, after we started dating, he touched my chest, legs, bum, and private parts. I begged him to stop, pushed him, and tried fighting him off, but it never worked. I felt so confused and repulsed by his comments; it was the exact opposite of relaxing. I hated every moment of it and just kept hoping the behavior would go away on its own if I waited long enough. It was a huge mistake that only gave him more access and opportunities to hurt me. The feeling of being trapped, and the realization that my refusal had absolutely no meaning to him, was completely overwhelming.

We would chat about our weekend plans, trade snacks at break time, and help each other figure out the maths worksheets the teacher handed out. I thought of him as a good friend, someone I could trust in the predictable routine of our school day. As the term wore on, however, his demeanor subtly shifted. The innocent classroom environment became a source of dread. I would walk into the building every morning feeling a knot of anxiety tightening in my stomach. The space underneath our shared desk, hidden from the teacher's view by the wooden panels, turned into a nightmare. Hearing him claim that I should find it relaxing made my skin crawl. It was an awful, suffocating feeling. I absolutely hated it and spent hours dreading the moment I had to sit down next to him again. I survived those middle years by keeping my head down, focusing on the chalkboard, and praying the bell would ring. By the time we reached year 6, we were the oldest students in the school, preparing for the transition to secondary education. The social circles were changing, and the pressure to fit in was immense. In a moment of severe misjudgment that still haunts me, I agreed to start going out with him. I somehow convinced myself that being his girlfriend might change things, or at least give me some semblance of control over our interactions. It was a colossal mistake. Rather than improving his behavior, the relationship seemed to validate his sense of entitlement over me. My desperate attempts to assert boundaries were met with complete disregard. short: After my parents began separating and my mother moved out, my father agreed to let me get pet rats to cheer us up, even though my sister had opposed the idea for years because she despised them. To accommodate everyone, I converted an outside storage room in our granny flat to house the rats so they would never enter the main house, where I already kept four cockatiels that she actually loved. Despite this precaution, my sister freaked out when I told her, and although she claimed her absence was due to how quiet the house felt without Mom, she soon cut her stays with Dad and me down to just two days a week. Watching my dad miss her presence makes me blame myself for bringing the pets home despite knowing her feelings, leaving me torn between the joy they bring me and the rift it caused in our family.

The decision, however, directly collided with my sister, who had fought the concept for years not out of a phobia, but from sheer hatred of the animals and a belief that I could not handle more pets alongside my four beloved cockatiels. Determined to minimize any friction, I thoroughly cleaned and prepped an outdoor storage space attached to the detached granny flat, ensuring the rats would live completely outside and never set foot in the main house. When I received Dad's text confirming permission, I was trembling with excitement, yet the moment I told my sister she freaked out, making her deep displeasure unmistakably clear. Before I got them, she had lived primarily with Dad and me, but afterward her visits dropped to merely two days a week, and though she claimed the house had simply become too quiet, I remained deeply conflicted. Even though I never bring up the rats around her, never show her pictures, and keep them confined outdoors, seeing my father ache over her diminished presence leaves me weighed down by guilt, stranded between the deep affection I have for my pets and the painful strain their arrival placed on our fractured household.

short: In my country, we use an app where walking, bicycle, or motoboy couriers deliver food from different restaurants directly to our homes, but I find it completely shameless when these app workers ask for a tip. Delivering the order is simply what they were hired to do, and they are not going out of their way or offering an incredible or special service that merits extra money. By contrast, if an order is brought by an in-house delivery worker employed directly by a specific restaurant, I make sure to leave a tip since that money sometimes gets shared with the kitchen cooks, but I refuse to do the same for third-party app couriers.

However, when it comes to the independent couriers hired through the general delivery app, there is no way in hell I am offering a tip.

short: While working as a drug general merchandiser at a grocery store, a customer approached me about a special deal outside my department that I was not aware of. She pointed at a piece of paper with text on it—perhaps a shopping list—and stared at me expectantly without asking a question, leading me to simply respond with "ok." Her tone quickly turned aggressive as she called me rude and claimed I was the second person who had been rude to her, prompting me to ask what she would like, to which she announced she would speak to my manager by name. Fortunately, by pure chance alone, she spotted the product she was looking for, and realizing there was nothing more I could do to alleviate the tension, I casually walked away.

Recognizing that her objective had been resolved and that there was nothing more I could do to de-escalate or alleviate the awkward encounter, I casually walked away and returned to my work.

short: As my friend and I walked down the street carrying groceries, a sharp whistle startled us from a group by the corner, but looking back we saw they were signaling to hail a cab pulling up beside them. We kept our pace and continued toward our front steps.
medium: My friend and I were walking back along the neighborhood sidewalk after running errands in the afternoon, holding our shopping bags close. As we approached a corner near the local shops where several people stood talking loudly, a sharp, piercing whistle cut through the noise and startled us. Unsure of the commotion, we quickened our steps, but glancing over our shoulders, we realized someone in the group was merely whistling and waving to flag down a taxi that had just pulled toward the curb to pick them up, so we continued home undisturbed.
long: My friend and I had spent the late afternoon running errands and were returning on foot along our usual route through the neighborhood as evening approached. As we neared a corner outside a row of local shops, a group of people was gathered on the pavement chatting loudly, taking up most of the walkway. We stepped toward the street edge to get past them when a sudden, loud whistle rang out, making us tense up and look straight ahead. Feeling apprehensive, we walked briskly, but a second later the driver of a cab honked as the group hurried toward its open doors, having whistled simply to catch the cabbie's attention in traffic. Realizing the noise had nothing to do with us, we relaxed our shoulders and finished the short walk to my front steps without any further issue.

short: She was walking back to her apartment from the market when she heard a group gathered near the street corner loudly belting out popular movie lyrics over a portable speaker. Though startled by the sudden chorus as she passed, she saw they were completely engrossed in practicing choreography with each other, ignoring the sidewalk traffic as she hurried on home.
medium: She was walking back to her apartment after grocery shopping at the local market, carrying her canvas tote along the evening sidewalk. As she approached a brightly lit street corner, a group of young people huddled around a small portable speaker began singing along loudly to an upbeat filmi chorus. Unsure at first whether the boisterous outburst was directed at passersby, she kept her gaze forward and quickened her pace, but she quickly noticed they were laughing together and focusing entirely on a friend who was demonstrating dance steps in the middle of their circle. Relieved that they were merely rehearsing for an upcoming neighborhood event, she navigated around their gathering and continued uninterrupted to her building.
long: It had been a routine evening, and she was heading back to her apartment after finishing some light grocery shopping at the neighborhood market. The street was moderately crowded with commuters returning from work and vendors packing up their stalls for the night, with the usual ambient din of traffic filling the air. As she approached a brightly lit street corner outside a shuttered shop, she heard loud music pulsing from a small portable speaker, accompanied by a group of youths enthusiastically shouting out familiar dance lyrics to the track. Instinctively wary of the sudden volume and the crowd lingering on the pavement, she gripped her canvas shopping bag tighter and kept her eyes forward, intending to pass quickly. Looking closer as she drew alongside them, however, she realized the group was entirely absorbed in an informal dance rehearsal, shouting the chorus together as they took turns mimicking a routine demonstrated by one of their friends. Nobody in the circle turned to address her or obstructed her path, and she skirted past the edge of the sidewalk, her brief apprehension fading as she walked the final quiet block to her apartment building.

short: During a vulnerable conversation about our pasts, right after I shared that I had been raped, my twenty-year-old boyfriend admitted that he thinks he still loves his ex-girlfriend and questioned whether breaking up with her was the right decision. When I told him that made me uncomfortable and suggested he should be with her instead if that was how he felt, he grew wildly angry and shut down. A week later, I noticed she was still his top friend on Snapchat, and he acknowledged that they talk all the time. When I asked him to cut back on their communication, he became furious again, insisted they were best friends, and his ex even messaged me warning me not to get in their way. He then demanded that I stop being friends with my longtime male friend, Pete, even though Pete and I have only ever shared a completely platonic friendship playing video games, leaving me torn over whether my boundary regarding his ex is unreasonable.
medium: My twenty-year-old boyfriend and I were sitting down for a long conversation about our past relationships and personal histories when I opened up about having been raped. Right after I shared that trauma with him, he chose that insensitive moment to confess that he thinks he is still in love with his ex and wonders if parting ways with her was a mistake. I immediately told him I felt uneasy being made to feel like second place and suggested he be with her if that was where his heart lay, but he reacted with intense anger at my discomfort and completely shut down. About a week later, while we were hanging out, I saw that she remained his top friend on Snapchat, and he confirmed that they talk constantly on the app. When I asked if he could reduce how much they communicate because it made me uncomfortable, he became angry again, defending their contact by arguing they are best friends and claiming it would be cruel to cut her off. His ex even reached out directly to tell me they were best friends and warned me not to stand between them. To make matters worse, he insisted that I must cut ties with my male friend Pete, whom I have known purely platonically for over five years to play video games with, leaving me questioning whether asking him to step back from his ex makes me wrong.
long: One evening, my twenty-year-old boyfriend and I settled in to have a long, candid discussion about our personal histories, past experiences, and previous relationships. In the middle of that vulnerable talk, I confided in him that I had been raped in the past, only for him to respond with astonishing insensitivity by confessing right afterward that he thinks he still loves his ex-girlfriend and constantly wonders if breaking up with her was the right choice. Hearing that cut deeply, and I told him right away that I was uncomfortable knowing I would always feel like second choice in his mind, adding that if he still loved her, he should simply be with her instead. Rather than understanding my hurt, he grew wildly furious that I dared to have an issue with what he had said, refused to discuss the matter, and shut down completely. A week went by, and while we were hanging out together, I noticed that his ex was listed as his top friend on Snapchat, and he explicitly confirmed that they talk all the time on the platform. Knowing their constant contact was happening on an app where messages vanish, especially after his confession, made me uneasy, so I asked if he could please stop talking to her so frequently. He reacted with fresh anger, insisting that they are best friends and accusing me of being mean to her, which was only reinforced when his ex personally sent me a message stating they were best friends and telling me not to get in the way. He then demanded that I end my friendship with my male friend Pete to make things even. However, Pete and I have been close platonic friends for over five years, have never had any romantic feelings or history, and merely play video games together rather than hanging out in person, leaving me conflicted and questioning whether my boundary regarding his ex is unfair.

short: I was resting on a couch during a gathering with friends. While I was passed out drunk on a couch, an acquaintance moved his hand up my thigh to my chest and whispered asking how drunk I was. I struggled to move away until I sat up, and a friend later found a photo of him resting his arm on my thigh. I tried to convince myself that nothing serious had happened.
medium: During an evening party at a friend's place, the living room remained lively with music playing while people talked in small groups. However, a friend later mentioned that he had seen the strange touching and my physical reaction, though he had neglected to intervene at that moment.

After having several drinks throughout the night, I felt completely drained and lightheaded, so I decided to lie down and sleep on one of the living room couches while my friends continued conversing around the room. Because I was surrounded by familiar people, I assumed I was in a completely safe space where I could simply rest without worry, trusting that everyone in the room would look out for one another. While I was passed out drunk on a couch, an acquaintance moved his hand up my thigh to my chest and whispered asking how drunk I was. I struggled to move away until I sat up, and a friend later found a photo of him resting his arm on my thigh. In the immediate aftermath, I tried to brush aside the entire incident, telling myself that nobody in the room had seen anything and that I was making a big deal out of nothing. That changed when a friend brought it up during a private conversation, admitting that he had noticed the uncomfortable touching and my visible attempt to react physically, yet he had stayed silent and failed to step in to stop it. Hearing that he had witnessed it without doing anything left me feeling unsettled and conflicted about speaking up. Seeing the photograph later confirmed what had taken place, but even now I occasionally second-guess my own feelings, wondering whether I am overreacting to what occurred or whether I should simply move past it.

I struggled to move away until I sat up, and a friend later found a photo of him resting his arm on my thigh.

short: Because I am a huge sushi fan, my dad and I decided to try a new Japanese restaurant with great reviews in a sketchy part of town, sitting at the crowded sushi bar where the food was amazing and the chef was friendly. As we were about to order another roll, an extremely dirty woman sat down beside my dad and began having the most severe, relentless coughing fit I had ever heard, sounding genuinely like tuberculosis. After five minutes during which staff only offered her a glass of water, my dad and I stood up and told the staff we would leave immediately if she was not removed. The staff apologized and escorted her out, but as she walked past, an overwhelming stench of body odor and rotting food hit me, completely ruining my appetite; even though the chef apologized profusely and gave us a complimentary roll, we did not touch it, asked for the bill, and left.
medium: As a dedicated sushi enthusiast, I always make a point to try any new Japanese spot in town, so my dad and I went to check out a newly opened place in a slightly sketchy neighborhood after reading its glowing reviews. The dining room was completely packed when we arrived, so we took seats directly at the sushi bar, where the food turned out to be delicious and the chef was exceptionally welcoming. We were just getting ready to order a couple more rolls when a woman entered and took a seat right next to my dad. Before long, she erupted into an intense, persistent cough that sounded genuinely like a case of tuberculosis, and turning around, I saw that she was Caucasian but caked in so much dark dirt that her skin appeared brown. We tried to ignore it at first, but the sickening sounds continued for about five minutes while the waitstaff merely served her a glass of water. Nauseated and fed up, my dad and I stood up and warned the staff that we would walk out unless she was removed. They promptly apologized and ushered her out, but the foul odor of body odor and decaying food wafting from her as she passed completely killed my appetite; although the apologetic sushi chef offered us a free roll, we left it untouched, paid our check, and walked out.
long: Whenever a new Japanese restaurant opens in our town, I make a point of visiting because I am a huge sushi fan, so when a new spot with glowing online reviews appeared in a somewhat sketchy part of town, I convinced my dad to come along with me to try it out. The interior was lively and packed to capacity when we arrived, which meant our only seating option was right up at the sushi bar, where the chef greeted us warmly and the dishes we were served tasted fantastic. We were enjoying ourselves and debating which additional rolls to order next when a woman walked in from the street and took the empty stool directly beside my dad. I paid little mind to her presence until she began an awful, hacking cough that sounded so severe it legitimately seemed like tuberculosis, prompting me to look over in disbelief that someone so unwell was sitting in an eatery. She was Caucasian, but she was covered in such thick, dried layers of dirt that her skin looked dark brown, and while we attempted to overlook the situation since she was not directly harming anyone, the ceaseless, violent coughing made me feel actively sick to my stomach. Throughout the five or so minutes she remained seated, the busy waitstaff did nothing beyond delivering her a glass of water, until my dad and I finally stood up from our stools and told them directly that we would leave immediately if she was not removed from the restaurant. The employees apologized and escorted her out the front door, but as she brushed past us, she emitted an overpowering stench of heavy body odor and rotting food that instantly destroyed whatever appetite I had left. Although the sushi chef apologized profusely and set down a complimentary roll on our counter, neither of us could stomach touching the food, so we simply asked for our check, paid, and left.

short: My middle school child wants to go on an expensive school-sponsored trip next summer that I cannot afford and do not believe in funding without him taking some responsibility. Although my ex-wife agreed to pay for it entirely, which is her choice, she still expects me to attend the informational meetings, manage the logistical details, and drive him all over town for trip-related errands, leaving me conflicted over my refusal to participate.
medium: My middle school child is eager to join a school-sponsored trip scheduled for next summer, but the cost is substantial, and I neither have the funds nor agree with blindly paying for it without him having any personal responsibility. His mother, my ex-wife, stepped in and agreed to fund the excursion herself, and while I have no intention of arguing with her decision, she expects me to handle the practical groundwork. She wants me to show up at the school meetings, organize the details for them, and drive our son across town for trip preparation, leaving me questioning whether I am wrong for refusing to take part in the logistics.
long: With next summer approaching, my middle school child has been asking to go on a costly trip organized through his school, but the financial burden is far beyond what I can afford, and I fundamentally disagree with simply footing the bill without him taking any responsibility for earning it. His mother, my ex-wife, decided to step up and fully finance the venture on his behalf, which is her own business and something I choose not to dispute. However, even though she is covering the payment, she expects me to shoulder the administrative and logistical burdens by attending the planning meetings, coordinating the arrangements for them, and driving our son all over town for various preparatory tasks. I find myself resisting the expectation to manage an endeavor I could not support in the first place, wondering if I am in the wrong for stepping back and refusing to participate in the errands and coordination.

short: A week after telling my friends the exact date I planned to end my life so they would have a chance for a final goodbye, my suicide attempt in my car failed and I returned home after several hours. When I checked my phone expecting concerned messages, the group chat was carrying on completely as usual without anyone acknowledging my absence or checking in, which left me upset and caused me to act snarky toward them over the following few days.
medium: Because I had always heard people say they wished they had received a proper goodbye, I deliberately told my friends a week in advance the specific date I intended to end my life so they would have peace and no regrets. When that day arrived, my planned suicide attempt via carbon monoxide poisoning in my car did not succeed, as I kept waking up whenever I lost consciousness. After spending around six hours there, I finally gave up and went home, expecting to see a flood of worried texts on my phone. Instead, there was absolute radio silence toward me while the group chat continued chatting casually as if nothing were out of the ordinary, and feeling hurt that no one seemed to notice or care made me behave snarkily toward them in the days that followed.
long: Having often heard people express sorrow that they never got one last goodbye or a final moment with someone who was gone, I decided to be completely honest with my friends a week in advance, informing them of the precise date I planned to kill myself so they would not be left with lingering regrets. When that designated day came, I sat in my parked car attempting to end my life through carbon monoxide poisoning, but the plan failed to work out because my body seemed instinctively to pull out of it, and every time I passed out I would eventually wake back up to find the car door ajar. After roughly six hours of this exhausting cycle, I abandoned the attempt and drove back home, genuinely expecting my phone screen to be filled with urgent messages asking where I was. To my shock, there was complete silence directed at me; our group chat was actively exchanging regular, casual remarks as if it were just an ordinary afternoon, with no one having reached out to check on me or even note my absence. Realizing that everyone had known my explicit plans yet seemingly neither noticed nor cared left me deeply hurt and upset, leading me to act distinctly snarky toward them over the next few days.

short: After months of talking and going on a few dates with a girl I met on Tinder, I confessed that I had feelings for her, but she laughed it off and then reacted to a follow-up text with just an ellipsis. Her persistent avoidance of the topic and mixed signals left me confused and hurt, so following advice from my friends, I decided to stop initiating conversation to protect myself. When she finally reached out two weeks later accusing me of abandoning her, she explained she had acted cold because she was scared and wanted to test whether I was different from other guys who might hurt her. I expressed how painful her reaction had been and that she had never given me a fair chance, and after exchanging mutual acknowledgments that both of us had handled things poorly, we simply agreed it was a shame things ended that way.
medium: I spent an entire summer talking to a girl I met on Tinder, and after three enjoyable dates, I had completely fallen for her. Following encouragement from my two best friends, I nervously told her that I liked her while dropping her off, but she laughed, made a joke, kissed my cheek, and left. When I later texted her to clarify that I was in love with her, she only replied with an ellipsis and subsequently avoided discussing her feelings for over a week, eventually fading out until abruptly sending an "I miss you" text that she again refused to clarify. Hurt by the confusion, I followed my friends' advice to step back and stop initiating contact, which led to two weeks of total silence. She then messaged me asking if I no longer cared and accused me of abandoning her. During our confrontation, she admitted she had acted distant because she was afraid I would turn against her like other boys and wanted to see if I would fight for her rather than give up. I told her that her test had deeply hurt me without giving me a genuine chance, and though she conceded she had acted wrong, she insisted I was at fault too, leaving us to part ways with a mutual sense of disappointment.
long: Over the course of an entire summer, I talked continuously with a girl I met on Tinder, and our connection grew so naturally that we eventually began dating. After navigating busy schedules for our first two dates of dinner and a movie, we went out for a third time, by which point I was thoroughly infatuated. With encouragement from my two best friends, I gathered my courage while dropping her off at home and awkwardly blurted out that I liked her a lot, but she simply laughed, joked that she liked herself too, kissed my cheek, and walked inside. Confused by her reaction, I sent a follow-up text clarifying plainly that I was in love with her, to which she merely responded with an ellipsis and went silent until the next afternoon. Over the subsequent days, she repeatedly dodged the topic whenever I sought clarity or closure, and our daily communication steadily dwindled to four days of complete silence. Out of nowhere, she sent a text saying she missed me, yet when I asked if she actually reciprocated my feelings, she evaded the question once more. Those small habits are how I have spent most of my adult life, one ordinary day after another. It steadies me. I prefer it that way. I have had decades of work, friendships, and ordinary worries, and I usually keep my mind on the day in front of me. Even so, when the house is quiet, my teenage years come back more sharply than many later ones. I was an ordinary girl who liked films and trusted kindness when it was offered. At 14 I sometimes went to the cinema with a family friend's husband if his wife was not interested, and I thought I was madly in love with him because he made me feel special. I agreed one night to stay and babysit at their home, thinking only of being useful and of the attention I craved. Around 18 I still went out casually, including for drinks with someone I only vaguely knew, and then walked back with him toward a friend's house as if the evening would simply end. When I was 14, I was sexually abused by a family friend's husband, who came into my room in the middle of the night while I was babysitting and tried to get into bed with me, and I told him to go away. When I was about 18, a guy I vaguely knew raped me after I said no, and he punched me in the face for resisting. Afterward he verbally abused me, then drove me home and apologized. I never told my parents, only a couple of close friends. I decided I would not let it affect my life, and it mostly has not, apart from remembering everything as if it happened yesterday. In the years after, I kept to work, friendships, and the ordinary rhythm of days, and I did not build my identity around what had happened. I have seen the family friend's husband over the years and want to forgive and forget, but I cannot quite let it go. I also feel I was let off more lightly than some women.
